title: Kapil Dev Lauds India's 'Much Better' Team After Asian Games Gold Over Pakistan
excerpt: The 1983 World Cup-winning captain congratulated the young Indian side after its 19-run win over Pakistan sealed a cricket double gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
body:
• Kapil Dev, India's 1983 World Cup-winning captain, congratulated the men's team after its 19-run win over Pakistan sealed Asian Games cricket gold on Saturday.
  • "We know our team is much better. We are playing better, and congratulations," the 67-year-old legend told ANI after the gold medal clash.
  • India's 211 for 6 beat Pakistan's 192 for 6, completing a double gold in cricket after the women's team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs — India's 19th gold of the Games.
  • Kapil also hailed Pranavi Urs, the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold, calling it a reflection of "talent, determination and hard work".

India's 1983 World Cup-winning captain Kapil Dev has congratulated the men's cricket team after it defeated Pakistan by 19 runs to win the gold medal at the Asian Games on Saturday, backing the young side's quality in the aftermath of the high-voltage final.

Speaking to ANI after India's victory in the gold medal clash at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, Kapil said he had full confidence in the team's abilities and praised its performance on the biggest stage in continental cricket.

"We know our team is much better. We are playing better, and congratulations. I think, all the best, good luck. And I know they are doing well and I have no doubt about that."

— Kapil Dev, 1983 World Cup-winning captain, to ANI

India posted 211 for 6 after winning the toss, powered by quickfire half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma, before restricting Pakistan to 192 for 6 to seal the title.

Context & Background

Abhishek Sharma lit up the powerplay with a 20-ball half-century — India's fastest fifty against Pakistan in T20Is — finishing with 61 off 28 balls, including seven sixes. Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 off 22 balls, with three fours and four sixes, carried India past 200 after the middle order briefly stuttered.

Pakistan's chase was anchored by Hasan Nawaz's superb 96 off 51 balls, with five fours and seven sixes, but India's spinners held their nerve. Washington Sundar (2 for 29) and Axar Patel delivered decisive spells, while Shivam Dube (2 for 33) broke a threatening 87-run stand by removing Saim Ayub for 29.

The victory completed a double gold in cricket for India. Earlier, Harmanpreet Kaur's women's team had beaten Sri Lanka by 147 runs to win its gold. The men's title was India's 19th gold of the Games and its 81st medal overall, alongside 26 silver and 36 bronze.

Impact & Analysis

Kapil's endorsement carries particular weight because the 1983 victory he captained transformed cricket's standing in India. His framing — that India was simply the better team and played like it — reflects how far the country's T20 depth has come: the Asian Games squad, led by Shreyas Iyer, is a second-string side missing most of the first-choice XI, yet it dominated Pakistan in a final.

As president of the Professional Golf Tour of India, Kapil also hailed a second landmark of the day: Pranavi Urs's individual golf gold, the first by an Indian woman at the Asian Games. The 23-year-old from Mysuru finished at 15-under 265, edging China's Yin Ruoning and Singapore's Shannon Tan by one stroke, while also anchoring India's team silver alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.

"Pranavi Urs' historic gold medal in the women's individual event and the silver medal won by our women's team at the Asian Games are moments of immense pride for India and Indian golf," Kapil said in a statement, praising her "nerves of steel and tremendous belief". It is India's first golf gold at the Games since Shiv Kapur's men's individual triumph in 2002.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the double cricket gold lands on a weekend when a parallel storyline — the ODIs against West Indies — also commands attention; the gold medals add a rare multi-sport dimension to Indian sporting pride, with cricket now contributing directly to the Asian Games tally.

What's Next

India's cricketers return to the white-ball calendar with momentum, while Kapil's comments will likely set the tone for the build-up to the next major ICC events: expectation, not hope, as the default setting for this generation of Indian cricketers.
